text: Hi Maria, it's Alex from financial aid at Westbrook State. Do you have Daniel's award letter handy?
I do, it's right here.

Great. His total aid package is $31,500. Before you get excited, that's a mix: $15,000 in grants, which are free money, $14,000 in loans, which get paid back, and $2,500 in work-study he earns at a campus job.
Okay, so the loans we pay back, and the grants we don't.
Exactly right.
Wait, is the Parent PLUS loan part of that $31,500?
Yes, it is. The Parent PLUS is $8,500 of the $14,000 in loans. It's in your name, it's optional, and it needs its own application and a credit check.
Got it, so that one would be mine to repay, and we can say no to it.
Right. Your SAI, the Student Aid Index, is a number calculated from your FAFSA. It's not what you'll pay, it's just used to figure out what he qualifies for.
Mm-hm, okay.
Daniel was also selected for verification. That's not an approval, it just means the school needs more paperwork, like tax return transcripts, by July 15.
So we still have to send the tax transcripts, and the deadline is July 15.
That's it. To keep the Westbrook Grant he needs SAP, Satisfactory Academic Progress: at least a 2.0 GPA and finishing 67 percent of the credits he attempts, every term.
Okay. He's a good student, so a C average shouldn't be a problem. What happens if he drops a class?
One dropped class is usually fine, as long as he still completes at least 67 percent of what he attempts that term.
Okay, that makes sense.
You'll accept or decline each award in the student portal. You'll get an email when it's submitted.
Mm-hm.
The net price is $23,000, that's the full $38,000 cost minus the $15,000 in grants.
Okay, so the $23,000 is what's left before loans and work-study, and the loans we pay back.
Exactly. Any other questions for me today?
No, I think that's everything. Thank you, Alex.
